agentCan: Create Cloud projects, OAuth clients, redirect URIs, and scope declarations via Google Cloud APIs (with authorized credentials)
Enable the Gmail/Drive/Calendar APIs in the API library
Draft per-scope justifications and the privacy-policy / homepage copy
Probe the console's Data Access page to confirm per-scope sensitivity labels

approval.cost: Free; the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes) is vendor-side with no fixed cost/duration in Google's docs
approval.trigger: Two gates: (1) Brand verification, required to show your name/logo on the consent screen (automated: usually minutes; manual: typically 2-3 business days; result valid 7 days, must publish within that window). (2) Scope verification: sensitive scopes typically 3-5 business days; restricted scopes potentially several weeks to months PLUS an annual CASA security assessment and annual re-verification.
approval.wait: Minutes to 2-3 days (brand); 3-5 business days (sensitive scopes); several weeks to months (restricted scopes)

blockers.detail: Apps showing the unverified-app warning are capped at 100 NEW users total over the project's lifetime (not resettable); the only appeal is completing verification. Separately, Testing publishing status limits you to 100 listed test users and their authorizations (including refresh tokens) expire after 7 days.
blockers.howToClear: Complete brand + scope verification before any real launch; stay in Testing only for internal pilots.
blockers.title: 100-user lifetime cap while unverified

blockers.detail: Restricted scopes (gmail.readonly/modify, full Drive, etc.) require an annual third-party CASA security assessment, a permitted application type, and annual re-verification. Google warns verification 'might require several months' depending on data sensitivity.
blockers.howToClear: Design around the narrowest scopes that avoid the restricted tier: gmail.send instead of gmail.compose, drive.file (per-file picker) instead of full Drive.
blockers.title: Restricted scopes trigger CASA assessment

blockers.detail: Adding redirect URLs/JS origins, changing the product name, adding sensitive/restricted scopes, or changing branding after approval all trigger re-verification; reviewer question round-trips go through email and can restart the clock.
blockers.howToClear: Freeze branding, URIs, and the scope list before submitting; batch changes.
blockers.title: Changes after approval restart verification

alternatives: Internal user type (only members of your own Workspace org; breaks the third-party use case)
flavor.recommended: OAuth 2.0 client (Web application) + External user type
flavor.why: External is the only user type that lets any Google account authorize. If your agent also calls Google MCP/Workspace tool endpoints, create a SEPARATE OAuth client with the 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' checkbox: some Google MCP endpoints only accept agentic client IDs. The tag grants no extra scopes; normal consent and verification still apply.

humanMust: Google login + 2FA and the initial Auth Platform clicks
Accept the Google API Services: User Data Policy checkbox
Verify domain ownership in Search Console (DNS/HTML proof)
Record the demo video (English, consent screen with correct app name, client ID visible in the address bar, each scope's functionality shown)
Reply to reviewer emails and click Verify Branding / Publish branding
name: Google
nuances: Scope tiers decide your timeline. Gmail: gmail.send is sensitive; gmail.readonly/modify/compose and full mailbox are restricted. Drive: drive.file (per-file picker) is non-sensitive and strongly recommended; full drive/drive.readonly are restricted. Calendar reading sits in the sensitive tier. Confirm per-scope labels in the console's Data Access page, as tiers can shift.
The unverified-app warning appears when code requests sensitive/restricted scopes not declared (or not yet verified) in the console; the two must match exactly.

Common rejection reasons: justification does not explain why the scope is necessary; scopes broader than the feature (reviewers push downscoping); scopes for unimplemented future features; consent-screen scopes differing from the verification submission.
The client secret is shown/downloadable only once at creation; rotate via 'Add Secret' if lost. OAuth clients inactive 6 months are auto-deleted (30-day email warning).

The homepage must be public, describe functionality, and cannot be just a login page or a store/social link; the privacy policy must live on the same domain as the homepage and match the console entry.
A Google Workspace admin can block your app via third-party-app access controls; that is outside your control.
prerequisites: A Google account and a Google Cloud project
A verified domain (Search Console, by a project Owner/Editor) for homepage + privacy policy
App name, logo (square 120x120, under 1MB), support email, developer contact emails
Your agent's authorized redirect URIs (HTTPS only, no raw IPs, no wildcards) and JS origins
The minimal scope list, checked against the sensitivity tiers

steps.detail: Create or select a Google Cloud project in the console. This holds the OAuth client, enabled APIs, and consent-screen configuration.

links.label: Get started with Google Auth Platform

steps.title: Create a Cloud project

steps.detail: Branding page: app name (distinct, not confusable with Google brands), user support email, developer contact emails, logo, homepage, privacy policy, and ToS URLs. Register Authorized domains FIRST; each domain's top private domain must be verified in Search Console by a project Owner or Editor. The homepage must be public and describe functionality; the privacy policy must be on the same domain.
steps.title: Configure branding and verify domains

steps.detail: Audience page: choose External user type (any Google account can authorize; Internal would restrict to your own Workspace org). Publishing status starts at Testing (100 test users, 7-day token expiry).
steps.title: Set External audience

steps.detail: Clients page: create an OAuth 2.0 client ID of type Web application. Add authorized redirect URIs (HTTPS only, no raw IPs, no wildcards, public-suffix TLDs) and JavaScript origins. The client secret is shown only once at creation; save it immediately. If you will call Google MCP/Workspace tool endpoints, create a second client with the 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' checkbox.
steps.title: Create the OAuth client

steps.detail: Data Access page: declare every scope your code will request; the console labels each non-sensitive, sensitive, or restricted. Strategy: prefer gmail.send over gmail.compose, drive.file over full Drive, and calendar read scopes; each restricted scope you add buys you weeks of review plus annual CASA. Enable the Gmail/Drive/Calendar APIs in the API library. Accept the User Data Policy ToS.
steps.title: Declare minimal scopes, enable APIs

steps.detail: Publish branding first (required before data-access verification). Then Verification Center > Prepare for verification: per-scope written justification plus an unlisted YouTube demo video showing the full OAuth grant in English, the consent screen with the correct app name, the client ID in the browser address bar, and each scope's functionality in use. Brand verification: minutes (automated) to 2-3 business days (manual). Sensitive scopes: typically 3-5 business days. Restricted scopes: several weeks to months, plus the CASA assessment and annual re-verification.
steps.time: Video + justifications ~2-4 hrs; waiting per tier above
steps.title: Submit brand and scope verification

tagline: The verification tiers are the whole story: brand check in days, sensitive scopes in about a week, restricted scopes in weeks to months plus an annual security assessment. Scope choice is timeline choice.

time.active: A few hours to 1-2 days (branding assets, domain verification, demo video, justifications)
time.total: ~1 week for sensitive-scope apps; weeks to months for restricted-scope apps
time.waiting: Brand: minutes to 2-3 business days; sensitive scopes: 3-5 business days; restricted scopes: several weeks to months (all stated by Google)
